title: Arrow-correspondence geometry for comparing slice and fiber cones
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the relative join of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], and cocartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A\subseteq C$ be a full subcategory of a quasicategory, all small in one sufficiently large universe. Let $K\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)$ be the full subcategory on arrows $a\to c$ with $a\in A$, with source $\pi:K\to A$ and target $u:K\to C$. Then $K$ is a quasicategory and $u$ is a cocartesian fibration. For $c\in C$ its fiber $K_c$ is a quasicategory. Put $I_c=A\times_C C_{/c}$, where an $n$-simplex of $C_{/c}$ is $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to C$ ending at $c$, projected by the entire initial face. Then $I_c$ is a quasicategory, and the slice diagonal $\psi_c:I_c\to K_c$ is an equivalence: it sends $\sigma$ to the arrow prism obtained by precomposing with $[n]\times[1]\to[n+1]$, $(j,0)\mapsto j$, $(j,1)\mapsto n+1$. It respects the source projections exactly. For $a\in A$, the identity arrow $1_a$ is final in $K_a$.
Put $J=K\star_C C$. There is a functor $S:J\to C$ with $Si_K=\pi$ (followed by $A\subset C$), $Si_C=1_C$, and $Sj_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}=k_c$, where $k_c:I_c^{\triangleright}\to C$ appends $c$. The identity-arrow map $\delta:A\to K$ and the relative join map $\delta\star1$ give a coherent transformation $\beta:i_K\delta\to i_C|_A$ with $S\beta$ the constant transformation of $A\subset C$.
For each $c$ define $T_c^+=i_Ck_c$ and $T_c^-=j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}$. Let $b:I_c^{\triangleright}\to\Delta^1$ take the base to $0$ and apex to $1$. The map $(b,k_c)$ lands in $A\star_C C\subseteq\Delta^1\times C$. Define $T_c=(\delta\star1)(b,k_c)$. There exist coherent transformations $\gamma_c^+:T_c\to T_c^+$ and $\gamma_c^-:T_c\to T_c^-$. Both components at the apex are $1_{i_C(c)}$. At a base vertex $e:a\to c$, the component of $\gamma_c^+$ is $\beta_a$, while the component of $\gamma_c^-$ lies in $i_K(K)$ and is the arrow from $1_a$ to $e$ represented by the square with source side $1_a$ and target side $e$. Thus its image under $\pi$ is $1_a$. No limit, colimit, coefficient category or lifting theorem is asserted here.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow correspondence and the constructions beta, T, gamma-plus, gamma-minus in its proof; Corollary 5.3.7.3 (0478), Theorem 4.6.4.19 and Corollary 4.6.4.20 (02VT), Proposition 4.7.3.20 (02J2). Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], the arrow simplicial set and its full subcategory $K$ are quasicategories. An inner-horn problem for $u$ adjoints to a map from $(\Delta^1\times\Lambda_i^n)\cup(\{1\}\times\Delta^n)$ to $C$. By [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product] its inclusion into $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne: apply that lemma to the inner horn and $\{1\}\subseteq\Delta^1$. Fill in $C$. Every source vertex belongs to the horn, hence to $A$; fullness puts the filler in $K$. Thus $u$ is an inner fibration. Given $e:a\to c$ and $v:c\to c'$, fill their inner $2$-horn to obtain $h:a\to c'$ and the composition triangle. With the degenerate source triangle this gives a square $s:e\to h$ in $K$ with source side $1_a$ and target side $v$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text: Fix $z:b\to d$ in $K$. Set $V=\operatorname{Map}_C(a,b)$, $Z=\operatorname{Map}_C(a,d)$, $Y=\operatorname{Map}_C(c,d)$ and $Y'=\operatorname{Map}_C(c',d)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] and fullness, $\operatorname{Map}_K(e,z)\simeq V\times_Z^hY$ and $\operatorname{Map}_K(h,z)\simeq V\times_Z^hY'$, with the endpoint projections respected. Here $V\to Z$ postcomposes with $z$, and the other maps precompose with $e,h$. The composition triangle and [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] give the specified homotopy $e^*v^*\simeq h^*$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting] to the diagram with top row $V\times_Z^hY'\to V\times_Z^hY\to V$ and bottom row $Y'\xrightarrow{v^*}Y\xrightarrow{e^*}Z$. The right square and outer rectangle are their defining homotopy-pullback squares, so the left square is a homotopy pullback. Naturality and endpoint compatibility in the arrow-mapping lemma identify it with the mapping square for $s$ over $v$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], $s$ is $u$-cocartesian. The definition [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] gives the required cocartesian fibration. A horn in the strict fiber $K_c$ is a lifting problem for this inner fibration over the constant simplex at $c$, so its filler stays in the fiber and $K_c$ is a quasicategory.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text: Write $S_c=C_{/c}$ and $E_c=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,C)\times_C\{c\}$. The prism formula and the equivalence $\delta_c:S_c\to E_c$ over $C$ are exactly [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence]. The source maps $S_c\to C$ and $E_c\to C$ are right fibrations by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to $\delta_c$: its map on each strict source fiber is a homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes. Pull back the two right fibrations and this map along $A\subseteq C$. Right-horn lifting is preserved by a degreewise pullback: compose a lifting square with $A\to C$, fill it in the original right fibration, and pair that filler with the given simplex in $A$. The resulting source fibers are unchanged. The fiberwise equivalence criterion in [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation] gives a simplicial homotopy inverse over $A$ to the pulled-back map $\psi_c:I_c\to K_c$. Every vertex component of these homotopies is in a strict source fiber, hence in a Kan complex by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. All its edges are equivalences: the two outer $2$-horn fillers give inverse edges and their inverse triangles. Thus [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] turns the two homotopies into coherent natural equivalences, and $\psi_c$ is an equivalence of quasicategories. Both pullbacks are quasicategories, since they are full subcategories of $S_c,E_c$: a simplex lies in the pullback precisely when all its source vertices belong to $A$, equivalently its entire source face lies in $A$. The prism leaves that face unchanged, proving the exact equality of source projections. No assumption that $A$ is closed under equivalences of objects of $C$ is used.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, slice diagonal restriction; Theorem 4.6.4.19 and Corollary 4.6.4.20 (02VT).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final], the identity $1_a$ is final in $C_{/a}$. The source restriction $I_a$ is a full subcategory containing it. Its right-pinched mapping spaces into $1_a$ equal those in $C_{/a}$: every vertex of a defining mapping simplex is one of its two endpoints, so fullness includes every such simplex. They are therefore contractible, and $1_a$ is final in $I_a$. The equivalence $\psi_a$ of step 3 takes this vertex to the identity-arrow vertex of $K_a$. Equivalences induce equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Precomposition with an equivalence edge is a homotopy equivalence of mapping spaces by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] (its component class is invertible, and composition is associative and unital up to homotopy). Applying a quasi-inverse and its unit and counit therefore identifies the mapping space from any object of $K_a$ into this vertex, up to equivalence, with a mapping space into $1_a$ in $I_a$. It is contractible, which is precisely finality in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. This does not assume that $a$ is final in $C$.

Form $J$, its inclusions and $j_c$ by [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-join-cartesian-realization] to $u^{\mathrm{op}}:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to C^{\mathrm{op}}$ and reverse vertex order: the opposite of $C^{\mathrm{op}}\star_{C^{\mathrm{op}}}K^{\mathrm{op}}$ identifies with $J$. Reversal sends an inner horn of index $j$ to the inner horn of index $n-j$, so opposites preserve quasicategories. Hence $J$ is a quasicategory. Apply [lem-coef-arrow-prism-collage-inner-anodyne] with $X=C$ and $B=K$ to obtain its explicitly defined $P,Q$, evaluation $Q\to C$, and simplicial diagonal $d:J\to P$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text: Let $H\subseteq J$ be the union of the images of $\delta\star1:A\star_C C\to J$ and all $j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}$. Here $\delta$ takes a source simplex to its prism constant in the arrow direction. These maps are injective: identity prisms recover their source, and a slice prism contains a maximal chain surjecting onto its defining simplex. Prescribe $P_H\to C$ in the notation of [lem-coef-arrow-prism-collage-inner-anodyne]. On an identity-arrow support with coordinate $\sigma$, send both $s_j,t_j$ to index $j$ of $\sigma$. On a slice support with base $\tau:\Delta^{i+1}\to C$ ending at $c$, send $s_j$ to $j$ and every $t_l$ to $i+1$, followed by $\tau$. These are monotone formulas and agree with the evaluation on $Q$. They agree on overlaps: an identity prism with constant target has constant source, and the surjective maximal chain forces the slice simplex to be constant too. Pure-factor values are the source projection and identity. The same index formulas commute with simplex operators, including removal of a whole block. Thus they give a map $Q\cup P_H\to C$.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-arrow-prism-collage-inner-anodyne], $Q\cup P_H\hookrightarrow P$ is inner anodyne. Since $C\to\Delta^0$ is an inner fibration, its defining lifting property extends the prescribed map to $F:P\to C$. Set $S=Fd$. On pure factors, $d$ is the source chain or target chain, so $Si_K=\pi$ and $Si_C=1_C$. On a slice-cone support its chain is $s_0<\cdots<s_i<t_{i+1}<\cdots<t_n$; the prescribed indices $0,\ldots,i,i+1,\ldots,i+1$ give exactly $k_c$. Hence $Sj_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}=k_c$. On an identity-arrow support all chain indices remain their original indices, so $S(\delta\star1)(\epsilon,\sigma)=\sigma$ exactly.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text:
The simplicial map $\delta$ sends every simplex of $A$ to its prism constant in the arrow direction. The induced relative-join formula of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join], applied to $A\star_A A=\Delta^1\times A$, defines $\beta$. Its endpoints are $i_K\delta$ and $i_C|_A$, and the last equation of step 7 makes $S\beta$ constant. Since $A$ is full, $A\star_C C$ identifies with the full simplicial subset of $\Delta^1\times C$ whose vertices over $0$ lie in $A$. Thus $(b,k_c)$ factors through it and defines $T_c$. Define $\gamma_c^+$ on $\Delta^1\times I_c^{\triangleright}$ by sending $(t,w)$ to
$$(\max\{t,b(w)\},k_c(w))\in A\star_C C$$
and then applying $\delta\star1$. Maximum is monotone, so this is a simplicial map. At $t=0,1$ it gives $T_c,T_c^+$. Its base-vertex component is $\beta_a$ and its apex component is the identity.

source.place: Proposition 7.3.5.5, arrow-correspondence geometry; retained proof route.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-slice-cone-prism-simplicial] with $X=C$ and the chosen $c$. Restrict its map $G$ to $\Delta^1\times I_c^{\triangleright}$. Its source prism is always the initial face of the slice simplex, independently of the interval parameter. All source vertices therefore lie in $A$, and fullness makes the initial arrow prism lie in $K$ in every degree. Thus $G$ restricts to a map into $J$. At parameter $0$, its prism is an identity prism and its target coordinate is $k_c$, giving precisely $T_c$. At parameter $1$, its prism is the slice diagonal and its target coordinate is constant at $c$, giving $j_c\psi_c^{\triangleright}=T_c^-$. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this simplicial map is a coherent transformation $\gamma_c^-:T_c\to T_c^-$. The prism lemma gives its constant apex edge and its square at $e:a\to c$, whose source side is $1_a$ and target side is $e$. Hence that component lies in $i_K(K)$ and its image under $\pi$ is exactly $1_a$. Together with step 8 this proves all the requested component conditions.
